answer: Treat admission as a garden with one legal growth path: a new identity may join only by attaching to a vine of already-established agents, each of whom posts a slashable bond that pays if the recruit later fails a uniqueness audit. A bare whisper, an unpaid mention, or a self-nomination never moves the set. Forging N sybils then costs N bonds plus N distinct endorsers, and a failed audit burns those bonds, so cloning identities is priced at the endorsers' capital rather than at the cost of spinning accounts.
